category_title: Students who engage in disruptive behavior to avoid difficult academic tasks
minimal_context: David is presented with a reading assignment during his English Language Arts class.
dialogue:
TUTOR: David, it is time for ELA. Please read this passage and complete the assignment at your desk.

STUDENT: (Stares at the paper) I'm not reading this. It's too long.

TUTOR: You need to do your work. Just get started.

STUDENT: (Pushes the assignment off the desk) No! I'm not doing it.

TUTOR: David, pick up your paper right now or I will have to send you to the office.

STUDENT: I don't give a s***! Send me to the office, I'm not doing this f***ing reading!

options.A: Provide a ticket for each behavioral expectation met, which can be exchanged for a break or an item from the classroom treasure box.
options.B: Adjust the ratio of lower-level to higher-level reading questions on the assignment, keeping the percentage of lower-level questions highest for the student.
options.C: Allow the student to choose his own creative reading projects based on his individual strengths and personal interests during the ELA period.
options.D: Create a classroom reading community founded on mutual respect for student choice and individual perspectives during ELA and other academic periods.
